short_def: Site slang, most often for an Inspector of Works (工程督察): a person who checks that works follow the contract, drawings, specifications and relevant legislation, usually assisting the engineer. In loose speech it may also be used for other inspecting or supervisory staff; that is not a 1:1 official-title mapping.
note: This is the starter example for the dictionary. HKIE Shi Chuan Hui cards gloss 幫辦 as 工程督察 / inspector of works. Career sites describe the post as a site inspector assisting the engineer, with a folk explanation linking the nickname to a Qing-dynasty deputy post (幫辦); that etymology is reported as folklore, not as historical proof. Do not collapse these official titles: Inspector of Works (工程督察, also Assistant / Senior Inspector of Works) is the usual official English/Chinese mapping; government Works Supervisor (監工; Works Supervisor I / II = 一級監工 / 二級監工) is a distinct and usually more junior works grade; Clerk of Works (工程監督) is a related but distinct official title, common on government or consultant resident-site-staff teams. 皇家佬 is slang for government works site staff, not a title. 幫辦 is not the contractor's 科文 (foreman). VTC's occupation listing also uses 工程檢查員 for Inspectors of Works; the civil-service grade name is 工程督察.
sources: HKIE-2012; CTGJ-2026; PONEWS-2; VTC-IOW; HAD-WG; HA-ABBR

alt_terms: IoW | IOW | Inspector of Works | AIOW | SIOW
short_def: A Hong Kong government works grade: technical staff who inspect and supervise works for conformity with the contract, drawings, specifications and relevant legislation.
note: Official civil-service / public-works title. Typical ranks include Assistant Inspector of Works, Inspector of Works, Senior Inspector of Works, and (in some departments) Chief Technical Officer (Inspector of Works). VTC also describes the occupation, and its Chinese listing uses 工程檢查員; the civil-service grade name is 工程督察. Distinct from Works Supervisor (監工) and from Clerk of Works (工程監督). Site slang 幫辦 is often used for this post, but 幫辦 is also used more loosely. Not a contractor 科文.

alt_terms: WS | Works Supervisor | WS I | WS II | 一級監工 | 二級監工
short_def: A Hong Kong government works grade, usually junior to Inspector of Works, providing technical assistance and carrying out site inspections. Ranks are Works Supervisor I and Works Supervisor II (一級監工、二級監工).
note: Official civil-service title. Distinct from Inspector of Works (工程督察) and from Clerk of Works (工程監督). In ordinary Cantonese 監工 can also mean supervising works in general, or loosely any supervisor; that everyday use is not the grade name. Some people may still call frontline government inspection staff 幫辦 or 皇家佬, but 監工 is not a synonym of those slang words or of Clerk of Works.

short_def: Site slang, originally for government works staff who visit or are stationed on a public-works site, typically an Inspector of Works (工程督察) or a Works Supervisor (監工).
note: CT Good Jobs restricts the term to government inspectors. A 2021 trade article says it mainly means civil-service inspectors on government jobs, but is sometimes extended to all client- or consultant-side inspectors. Xiaoluban glosses it as government inspector / Clerk of Works, and explains it as a government 工程督察 or 監工. Keep the core sense: slang for government (or, loosely, client-side) works inspection staff. It is not itself an official title. Do not treat 皇家佬 as a synonym of Clerk of Works (工程監督), Inspector of Works, or Works Supervisor, and do not confuse them with a contractor 管工 / 科文. The '皇家' nickname is historical (colonial-government works).

short_def: Site slang for an engineer, from a Cantonese rendering of English 'engineer'. Also written or said as N展.
note: Used for civil, structural, building-services / E&M and other engineers. Informal address; the formal title depends on the person's actual appointment (e.g. Resident Engineer, Authorized Person, RSE).

short_def: Site slang, from English 'foreman': the contractor-side supervisor who assigns work and watches progress.
note: VTC describes 地盤管工 as supervising, directing and coordinating workers, and checking materials, under a general foreman. Distinct from 幫辦 / inspector, who represent the client, consultant or government side. Also heard as 管工 in more formal speech.

short_def: Slang for the main contractor's head foreman, who oversees the site's trade gangs rather than only one trade.
note: CT Good Jobs: general foreman of the main contractor (大判). A 2021 article: the top of the foreman line. Xiaoluban lists the formal pair 總管工／大科文 = General Foreman. In other Hong Kong settings 老總 can simply mean a boss; on site it usually means this general-foreman role.

short_def: The sub-contractor, or the person running that sub-contract gang, on a Hong Kong site.
note: Often interchangeable with 拾仔. Works may be further sublet (判上判), giving 大判, 二判, 三判. The HKIE slang cards gloss 判頭 more loosely as 'contractor'; career and trade articles treat it as the sub-contractor. In speech 判頭 may mean the firm or the boss. See also 大判.

short_def: Another common slang name for a sub-contractor, used alongside 判頭.
note: HKIE cards: 拾仔 / 分判商 / sub-contractor. Same caveats as 判頭.

english: Main contractor (also first-tier contractor in a chain)
short_def: Usually the main contractor who holds the head contract; in talk about layered subletting it can also mean the first-tier contractor in the chain.
note: Hong Kong sites commonly use a 大判 / 二判 / 三判 chain. Xiaoluban: 大判／二判／三判 = main / 2nd-tier / 3rd-tier subcontractor structure, with 總承建商 as Main Contractor. CT Good Jobs also uses 大判 for the main contractor when defining 老總.

short_def: A sub-contractor employed by the main contractor or first-tier contractor in a layered subletting chain.
note: See 大判 and 三判／三沙.

short_def: A further sub-contractor in a 判上判 chain, below 二判.
note: HKIE cards list 三沙 as 三判. Further tiers are possible but these three names are the ones usually heard.

short_def: Slang variant of 三判, listed on the HKIE engineering slang cards as 三沙 / 三判.
note: Cross-reference 三判. Etymology is not clearly explained in the available sources.

short_def: On a construction site, the person who contacts and arranges workers' attendance (a ganger or informal labour organiser).
note: CT Good Jobs: 工頭, responsible for contacting and arranging workers. In general Hong Kong usage 蛇頭 also means a human smuggler; that general sense is not a construction title and should be distinguished clearly in any public glossary.

short_def: Slang for a surveying assistant who helps a surveyor or survey officer with field measurement and looking after instruments.
note: Attested in CT Good Jobs. Do not confuse with 蛇頭 (ganger) or 蛇佬 (cable puller).

alt_terms: 叻㗎 | 大力佬 | 飛模佬 | 鐵模佬 | 埋碼員
formal_zh: 索具工（叻㗎）／金屬模板裝嵌工
short_def: Site slang, from a rendering of English 'rigger' (also written 叻㗎): the official specified trade that slings and handles lifting of heavy loads and also erects or dismantles large metal formwork.
note: The official CIC / VTC occupation is one combined trade, 索具工（叻㗎）／金屬模板裝嵌工 (Rigger / Metal Formwork Erector), not two official titles. JobsDB treats 叻架佬／大力佬 as riggers and stresses that they need not be 'strong'; the name is from the trade. Xiaoluban lists 大力佬／飛模佬 as 索具工 covering both lifting gear and large metal formwork (also 鐵模佬). A 2021 article also equates 埋碼員 with 叻架佬, and elsewhere emphasises the metal-formwork side. Do not map this official trade to a general labourer (雜工 / CID) or to a crane operator (天秤手). One career article's wording 吊臂工人 is inaccurate. Some site speech uses 大力佬 loosely for a strong general labourer; that loose reading is recorded under 大力佬 sense 2, not under 叻架佬.
sources: JOBSDB-2018; CTGJ-2026; PONEWS-1; XLB; VTC-RFM; CIC-CWR

alt_terms: 叻架佬 | 叻㗎 | 飛模佬 | 鐵模佬
formal_zh: 索具工（叻㗎）／金屬模板裝嵌工
short_def: Site slang (with 叻架佬, 飛模佬, 鐵模佬) for the official specified trade 索具工（叻㗎）／金屬模板裝嵌工: slinging and lifting, and erecting or dismantling large metal formwork. There is no separate official title '大力佬'.
note: Official sources (VTC occupation dictionary; CIC specified-trade list) treat rigger and metal-formwork erector as one combined trade. JobsDB, CT Good Jobs and Xiaoluban all point at this trade; a 2021 workers' article emphasises the metal-formwork side and contrasts it with 釘板佬 (timber formwork). That is a usage emphasis, not a second official title, so it is not split out as a rival official sense. Do not force a 1:1 mapping onto general labourer (雜工 / CID) or crane operator. JobsDB notes the name (in the official-trade reading) is from the trade, not from being physically 'strong'. Some Hong Kong site speech also uses 大力佬 loosely for a strong general labourer; that is sense 2, with no official title. See sense 2.
sources: JOBSDB-2018; CTGJ-2026; XLB; PONEWS-1; VTC-RFM; CIC-CWR

english: Heavy general labourer (loose slang, not an official title)
short_def: In some Hong Kong site speech, 大力佬 is also used loosely for a strong general labourer (大力雜工), not only for the official rigger / metal-formwork trade in sense 1. There is no official title for this reading.
note: Locked as a loose-speech sense on owner site attestation of 25 November 2026 (Hong Kong Time). This is not a second official trade and must not be mapped 1:1 onto 雜工 / CID or onto a crane operator. Sense 1 remains the official specified trade 索具工（叻㗎）／金屬模板裝嵌工. Any public entry should show both senses and say only sense 1 has an official title.

short_def: Slang for the worker who pulls electrical cables, nicknamed because a cable is likened to a snake.
note: CT Good Jobs: 鋪電線的線佬 (cable puller). Distinct from 蛇頭, 蛇仔 and 蛇王.

short_def: Short site name for a safety supervisor, who helps carry out safety inspections and site safety measures.
note: Under the Factories and Industrial Undertakings (Safety Officers and Safety Supervisors) Regulations, a principal or specialist contractor must employ a safety supervisor for a construction site where it directly employs 20 or more workers (counting rules differ for principal vs specialist contractors). A 2021 article says 安督 are often the sub-contractor's safety-patrol staff, while 安全主任 is typically the main contractor's registered safety officer — this employer split is a common pattern, not a statutory definition of the two titles.

english: Safety Officer (often a Registered Safety Officer)
short_def: The official title for the person responsible for occupational safety and health on site: inspections, training and incident follow-up.
note: Registration as a safety officer is a statutory regime under the FIU (Safety Officers and Safety Supervisors) Regulations. Informal writing uses SO or RSO (Registered Safety Officer).

short_def: Slang for a site electrician who installs, tests, maintains or repairs electrical installations, including cable laying.
note: Statutory electrical work must still be carried out by a Registered Electrical Worker of the appropriate grade (see 註冊電業工程人員). Do not confuse the nickname with a registration grade.

short_def: Slang for the worker who sets out lines on site from the drawings, traditionally with an ink line, so other trades can build to line and level.
note: CT Good Jobs uses 墨王. A 2021 article uses 墨斗, also called 平水, for the person who opens lines on site, and notes that many older foremen came from this trade. Xiaoluban lists 平水佬 as leveller. Closely related names, not always strictly synonymous in every gang.

short_def: The site mechanic who installs, services and repairs plant such as fans, generators, cranes and pumps.
note: A 2021 article notes the character 偈 is pronounced like 解 (gaai2). CT Good Jobs: repairs plant and also helps with oil and belt changes.

short_def: On site, often used for a woman doing general or cleaning labour, typically associated with a yellow safety helmet.
note: Sources warn not to call every woman on site 阿姐: a female engineer, inspector or clerk will usually wear a white or other non-labour helmet. In general Cantonese 阿姐 is simply a form of address for a woman. Jyutping of 姐 as a familiar address is commonly ze2 (changed tone).

short_def: Site slang for a general labourer, likened to old police CID officers who handled every kind of case.
note: The comparison is to the former Royal Hong Kong Police Criminal Investigation Department nickname, not to current police ranks. Informal and slightly comic; some people may find it dated.

short_def: A respectful form of address on site, often used for client- or consultant-side inspectors, resident engineers and, in many cases, the main contractor's project manager or more senior staff.
note: A 2021 article: all resident supervisory staff and structural engineers are addressed as 阿Sir; main-contractor project managers and above often are too. This is address, not a job title. Do not assume the person is a police officer (another common Hong Kong use of 阿Sir).

short_def: A building professional registered under the Buildings Ordinance to coordinate private building works and submit plans to the Building Authority.
note: An AP may be a registered architect, a registered professional engineer (structural or civil), or a registered professional surveyor, subject to Buildings Department registration rules. Appointment is a statutory requirement for private building works, together with an RSE and/or RGE as appropriate. Cap. 123.

jyutping: zyu3 caak3 git3 kau3 gung1 cing4 si1
short_def: A structural engineer registered under the Buildings Ordinance, appointed for structural design and related statutory duties.
note: Cap. 123. Often referred to on site simply as RSE.

jyutping: zyu3 caak3 ngaam4 tou2 gung1 cing4 si1
short_def: A geotechnical engineer registered under the Buildings Ordinance, appointed where foundation, slope or other geotechnical elements require it.

jyutping: zyu3 caak3 gim2 jim6 jan4 jyun4
short_def: A person registered under the Buildings Ordinance to carry out prescribed inspections and supervise prescribed repairs under the Mandatory Building Inspection Scheme.
note: Not the same as a site 幫辦 / Inspector of Works. RI is a statutory MBIS title.

alt_terms: CoW | COW | Clerk of Works | RCOW
short_def: A client- or consultant-side inspector who checks workmanship, keeps records and witnesses tests, especially on government or resident-site-staff teams.
note: Official English title is Clerk of Works; official Chinese in Hong Kong government / Housing Authority usage is 工程監督. Resident Clerk of Works (RCOW / 駐地盤工程監督) when stationed on site. Related to, but not automatically identical with, slang 幫辦 or 皇家佬. Do not confuse 工程監督 (Clerk of Works) with 工程督察 (Inspector of Works) or 監工 (Works Supervisor): these are distinct official titles / grades. Chinese 工程監督 is also used more loosely in speech for supervisory staff.

jyutping: zyu3 dei6 pun4 gung1 cing4 si1
short_def: An engineer stationed on site for the client or consultant, supervising whether works follow the design and the contract.
note: Xiaoluban warns that this is a supervisory-side post and should not be confused with a contractor's site engineer, sometimes also abbreviated SE.

alt_terms: Resident Site Staff | 駐地盤監督人員
short_def: The client- or consultant-side staff stationed on site to supervise the works, as a team name rather than a single grade.
note: Xiaoluban: 駐地盤監督人員 / Resident Site Staff, the resident supervision team for the consultant or client. May include a Resident Engineer, Clerk of Works and others, depending on the contract. Not a contractor's site team, and not itself a civil-service grade name.

jyutping: sik1 jam6 gei6 seot6 jan4 jyun4
short_def: A person recognised under the Code of Practice for Site Supervision to carry out specified site-supervision duties, graded by qualifications and experience.
note: Used with the statutory Supervision Plan. Grades are often spoken as T1-T5. See Buildings Department Code of Practice for Site Supervision (2009, 2024 edition cited by Xiaoluban).

jyutping: zyu3 caak3 jat1 bun1 gin3 zuk1 sing4 gin3 soeng1
short_def: A contractor registered with the Buildings Department to carry out general building works and street works.
note: Distinct from a Registered Specialist Contractor (RSC), who is registered for a designated specialist category.

jyutping: zyu3 caak3 zyun1 mun4 sing4 gin3 soeng1
short_def: A contractor registered with the Buildings Department in a designated specialist category of building works.
note: See also RGBC. Specialist categories are defined by the Buildings Department.

short_def: A plumber licensed by the Water Authority to carry out inside-service or fire-service plumbing works under the Waterworks Ordinance.
note: WSD official title. Closely tied to Form WWO 46. Distinct from the general trade nickname 水喉佬, who may or may not be the licensed person signing the form.

jyutping: zyu3 caak3 din6 jip6 gung1 cing4 jan4 jyun4
short_def: A person registered with EMSD to carry out electrical work of a stated grade under the Electricity Ordinance.
note: Grades commonly discussed on site include A, B, C, H and R. Registration is applied for on EMSD Form 8. Distinct from the slang 電王.

jyutping: zyu3 caak3 siu1 fong4 zong1 zi3 sing4 baan6 soeng1
short_def: A contractor registered with the Fire Services Department to install, maintain or repair fire service installations and to issue the relevant certificates.
note: After completing relevant work, an RFSIC issues F.S. 251 (Certificate of Fire Service Installations and Equipment). See FS 251.

short_def: The professional who measures quantities, values variations and interim payments, and deals with contract-cost matters.
note: Standard Hong Kong professional title, used constantly in payment and VO discussions.

short_def: On the contractor side, the person usually in overall charge of programme, cost and site resources for the project.
note: A generic management title, not a Buildings Ordinance register. Sometimes addressed as 阿Sir.

short_def: The trade that cuts, bends and fixes reinforcement to the drawings and bar schedules.
note: One of the three core reinforced-concrete trades, with 釘板佬 and 石屎佬. The work is also called 紮鐵.

short_def: The timber-formwork carpenter who erects and later strikes timber forms to line and level.
note: Also called 釘板 or 粗木 in trade speech. Distinct from metal-formwork crews (鐵模／鋁模; sometimes called 大力佬 in one source).

short_def: The trade that places, vibrates and finishes concrete; the work is called 落石屎.
note: 石矢 is a more written variant of 石屎. See 石屎.

english: Bamboo scaffolder (also metal scaffolder in broader talk)
short_def: The trade that erects, alters and dismantles scaffolding, especially bamboo scaffolding, a characteristic Hong Kong trade.
note: Official occupation names distinguish bamboo and metal scaffolders; in loose speech 棚佬 may cover the scaffold gang generally. High-risk specified trade; silver-card training often required.

short_def: The trade that installs and maintains building pipework for cold and hot water, flushing, and often soil and waste.
note: The statutory signatory for Water Authority submissions is the Licensed Plumber (持牌水喉匠), which may or may not be the same person spoken of as 水喉佬 on the day.

short_def: The trade that builds manholes and lays underground drains.
note: Standard trade name in Hong Kong compiled drawing/trade glossaries.

short_def: The trade that plasters walls, soffits, floors and stairs to a finish.
note: Common Hong Kong trade nickname; 批盪 is the process.

short_def: The trade that lays wall and floor tiles, and often marble or similar finishes.
note: 瓦仔 is site speech for tiles.

formal_zh: 身份證、平安卡、建造業工人註冊證
english: The three documents required to work on a construction site
short_def: In recruitment and many trade explanations: Hong Kong Identity Card, Green Card (平安卡), and Construction Workers Registration Card.
note: Recruitment and career sources (CT Good Jobs, JobsDB 齊三寶, a 2021 workers' article) use this document sense: Hong Kong Identity Card, Green Card (平安卡), and Construction Workers Registration Card. A construction workers' union explainer uses the same three-document definition. This conflicts with two PPE senses: sense 2 (safety helmet, safety shoes, reflective vest) recorded in Xiaoluban and, as '基本個人防護三寶', in a JobsDB safety article; and sense 3 (helmet, safety harness, safety shoes), locked as Hong Kong site speech on owner site attestation of 25 November 2026, without a published HK source found in the earlier review pass that uses that exact name as 地盤三寶. All three senses are attested in use; do not merge them. See senses 2 and 3.

english: The three basic items of site PPE (helmet, safety shoes, reflective vest)
short_def: In some site and compiled-glossary usage: safety helmet, safety shoes and reflective vest (安全帽、安全鞋、反光衣) as the three essentials for entering a site.
note: Xiaoluban records this PPE trio as 地盤三寶, and notes that some people also include the Green Card. JobsDB describes the same three items as 基本個人防護三寶 (helmet, reflective vest, safety shoes) and lists a safety harness separately as other PPE. Recruitment ads saying 齊三寶 more often mean the three documents in sense 1. A third site-speech telling is helmet, safety harness and safety shoes (sense 3). Flag all three senses in any public entry; do not silently replace the vest with a harness, or the documents with PPE.

english: The three basic items of site PPE (helmet, safety harness, safety shoes)
short_def: In some Hong Kong site speech: safety helmet, safety harness and safety shoes (安全帽、安全帶、安全鞋) as the three essentials.
note: Locked as a third sense on owner site attestation of 25 November 2026 (Hong Kong Time). A published Hong Kong source that uses this exact trio under the name 地盤三寶 was not found in the earlier review pass: Labour Department lists helmet, shoes and harness as PPE without the「三寶」label, and JobsDB treats the harness as additional PPE beside the vest set in sense 2. The trio also resembles Mainland「施工三寶」lists (which may include 安全網). Do not merge with sense 1 (documents) or sense 2 (vest set). Public entries must show all three senses.

alt_terms: 平安咭 | 綠卡 | 綠咭 | Green Card
formal_zh: 強制性基本安全訓練證明書
english: Mandatory Basic Safety Training Certificate (Construction Work); commonly 'Green Card'
short_def: The certificate showing that a person has completed Labour Department-recognised mandatory basic safety training for construction work. Required for employment on construction work.
note: Labour Department official wording: 強制性基本安全訓練課程（俗稱「平安卡」／「平安咭」）. English 'Green Card' is ubiquitous on sites and in VTC materials. Validity is generally one to three years as marked on the card (default three years if unmarked). Renewal is by a recognised revalidation course. This is not a visa, and not the same as the Construction Workers Registration Card or the 銀卡 specified-trade course.

formal_zh: 建造工友（指定行業）安全訓練課程證明
english: Construction Workers (Specified Trade) Safety Training Certificate ('Silver Card')
short_def: The certificate for a specified-trade safety training course required for certain high-risk trades, commonly called the Silver Card.
note: Hong Kong Institute of Construction / CIC course title: 建造工友（指定行業）安全訓練課程（銀卡課程）. CT Good Jobs: about 12 high-risk trades (e.g. bar bending and fixing, bamboo scaffolding, lift mechanics) must be done by silver-card holders. An earlier informal article associated 銀卡 mainly with lifting and signalling; later notes point to the broader specified-trade scheme (including A12 rigging). Prefer the official course title. Not a substitute for the Green Card.

short_def: The registration card issued under the Construction Workers Registration Ordinance, which a registered construction worker must present when entering a site.
note: CIC administers registration. Skill work in a designated trade must be carried out by a registered skilled or semi-skilled worker in that trade (大工／中工). Not the same document as the Green Card, though expiry dates have at times been aligned under a joint arrangement mentioned by the Labour Department.

short_def: A construction worker registered as a skilled worker in a designated trade, normally holding a recognised trade test or equivalent qualification.
note: CIC / Construction Workers Registration Ordinance wording. Qualifications are typically CIC, former CITA or VTC trade-test certificates or other recognised qualifications. Contrast 中工 (semi-skilled) and 白紙 (inexperienced newcomer, not a registration grade).

short_def: A construction worker registered as a semi-skilled worker in a designated trade, normally holding an intermediate trade test or equivalent.
note: See 大工. Official English: Registered Semi-skilled Worker.

formal_zh: 密閉空間安全訓練證明
short_def: Informal name for the safety-training certificate required before working in a confined space.
note: A 2021 workers' article uses 密閉證. The underlying official course is Labour Department-recognised confined-space safety training, separate from the Green Card. Formal course titles should be preferred in any official-name display.

english: Inexperienced newcomer / worker without trade qualifications (slang)
short_def: Recruitment and site slang for a new, inexperienced worker, often one without a trade-test qualification.
note: JobsDB and workers' articles use it this way. Xiaoluban: inexperienced / no trade-cert worker. Not an official registration grade.

english: A worker who walks around but does little work (slang)
short_def: Recruitment slang for someone who wanders the site without doing useful work, like a penguin waddling about.
note: JobsDB explains 唔係企鵝 in job ads as 'will not just stand around'. CT Good Jobs flags 企鵝免問 as a recruitment phrase. Informal and pejorative: not a job title, and not neutral workplace vocabulary.

english: A worker who often attends one day and then disappears for two (slang)
short_def: In construction job-ad slang, someone with very irregular attendance ('on one day, off two'), not a Fire Services officer.
note: JobsDB and a 2021 article record this sense. The ordinary meaning remains 'firefighter'. Pejorative recruitment slang, not a job title. Any dictionary UI should show the slang sense with a clear disambiguation.

english: Someone who promises to turn up and then cancels (slang)
short_def: Job-ad slang for a person who agrees to come to work and then stands the employer up (放飛機). Not an aircraft pilot.
note: JobsDB uses 飛機師; a 2021 article also uses 機師 in the same sense. Pejorative recruitment slang, not a job title and not an aircraft pilot.

english: Someone slacking off or hiding from work (slang)
short_def: Common Cantonese, also used on site, for a person who slips aside to avoid work.
note: A 2021 article warns that 蛇王 can also mean a snake catcher in ordinary Cantonese. Distinct from 蛇頭, 蛇仔 and 蛇佬. Pejorative when used of a person slacking off.

english: Paid at the end of the working day
short_def: Labour slang meaning wages are paid on the same day after work ('wash hands and collect pay').
note: Explained in the JobsDB walkthrough of a typical job-seeking line: 洗手出糧 800 = day rate $800, paid that day.

short_def: Ordinary sandpaper, used for rubbing down surfaces.
note: A 2021 article records a second, figurative sense — see sense 2.

short_def: By extension, a certificate of education or qualification, because many Hong Kong certificates are printed on slightly rough paper.
note: A 2021 article. Context-dependent and informal. Do not use this sense in official correspondence.

english: A serious site accident, typically one involving a fatality (slang)
short_def: In one 2021 article, 飛土 means a serious construction accident, generally one in which someone has died.
note: PUBLIC DEFAULT: filter (content warning). Single informal source. The term is grim slang for a serious, typically fatal, site accident; record it factually if it is included, and do not embellish. Low confidence pending a second source. Unrelated to excavated spoil in the ordinary sense. Not a racial slur, but unsuitable as casual public-page vocabulary without a warning. Owner accepted this public default on 25 November 2026: filter (content warning).

short_def: The ordinary Hong Kong name for concrete. 石矢 is a common written variant.
note: Universal on Hong Kong sites. 落石屎 = to place / pour concrete. Xiaoluban notes workers sometimes write 石矢 as a slightly more formal-looking variant.

short_def: Hong Kong site name for cement, from a rendering of the English word.
note: Not the same as 石屎 (concrete, which already contains cement, aggregate and water).

short_def: A non-structural lean-concrete layer used to level and protect the formation before the structural concrete is placed.
note: HKIE cards: 草鞋底 / blinding layer. A 2021 article also uses 草鞋. Formal English: blinding (plain / mass concrete). Related drawing abbreviation: PCC.

short_def: Slang for deformed / high-yield rebar, so called because of the ribbed ('flowered') surface.
note: A 2021 article: also called 高拉力鐵, i.e. deformed bar. Contrast 光身鐵 (plain round bar). Drawing marks such as T16 for a 16 mm high-yield bar are standard on Hong Kong reinforcement drawings.

short_def: Mild or plain reinforcement with a smooth surface, as opposed to 花鐵.
note: Attested in a 2021 trade article.

english: Starter bars / reinforcement left for lapping
short_def: Bars left projecting from already-cast concrete so that the next pour can be lapped or connected.
note: Attested in a 2021 trade article.

english: Unscheduled spacer / distribution bars used to keep main bars in position
short_def: Small bars, often not shown on the drawing, used on site to help keep the designed spacing of the main reinforcement.
note: Single informal source (2021). Keep the definition close to that wording; medium confidence.

short_def: A small plastic stool-like spacer used to support a layer of reinforcement at the correct cover or layer height.
note: Attested in a 2021 article. Related: 飛碟 (cover spacer).

short_def: A disc-shaped spacer, often dark-coloured, used to maintain concrete cover to the bars.
note: A 2021 article describes it as a black spacer ensuring cover. The flying-saucer nickname is from the shape.

short_def: Site slang for plastic pipe or plastic tubing.
note: HKIE cards list 膠批 / 膠喉. Common in drainage and BSE pipework talk.

short_def: Site name for vitrified clay / earthenware pipe, also called 陶土管 or 缸瓦管.
note: HKIE cards: K批 / 陶土管 / 缸瓦管 / clay pipe. Jyutping of the letter K follows the usual Cantonese letter-name kei1.

short_def: Galvanized steel tube, so called because galvanizing is nicknamed 鹽水 ('brine') on site.
note: Related slang: 鹽水 = galvanizing; 浸鹽水 = hot-dip galvanizing at the works. Attested in a 2021 article. Very common in older plumbing and fire-service pipework talk.

short_def: On a construction site, 鹽水 often means galvanizing rather than literal salt water.
note: See 鹽水喉 and 浸鹽水. Ordinary Cantonese 鹽水 still means saline / salt water; sense depends on context.

short_def: Ductile iron pipe, usually spoken with the English initials, used for water and some fire-service mains.
note: Listed on the HKIE slang cards as DI pipe / ductile iron pipe. Standard materials term rather than metaphor slang.

english: Polystyrene chip / sheet (expansion or joint filler)
short_def: Slang for polystyrene sheet or chips, from the look of a prawn cracker.
note: HKIE cards: 蝦片 / 發泡膠片 / polystyrene chip.

short_def: Fine or leftover quarry material after screening, used or disposed of as fill or waste depending on the specification.
note: HKIE cards: 篩尾泥 / 篩屑 / scalping. A 2021 article: residue sand and stone from a quarry.

english: A proprietary or generic repair / patching cement (slang)
short_def: A loose site name for a compound cement used to patch walls.
note: A 2021 article calls it a generic name for a wall-repair compound cement. May allude to a product line; do not treat as a single official product name without a package in hand. Medium/low specificity.

english: Coarse stone aggregate used for backfill
short_def: A coarser stone used as backfill.
note: Single 2021 source. Medium confidence.

english: A white cementitious bonding / interface agent (slang)
short_def: Site name for a white interface or bonding agent, also called 英泥寶 in one article.
note: Single 2021 source; product identity is not pinned to one brand here. Medium confidence.

short_def: A blank (blind) flange used to close off a pipe end.
note: HKIE cards: 盲餅 / blank frange (sic, for blank flange).

short_def: The ordinary Hong Kong site word for a beam.
note: Xiaoluban: 陣 = beam; drawing marks B / BM. Warning: on survey drawings BM means benchmark. Both senses are also entered under the headword BM. Compounds are common: 主陣, 副陣, 門頭陣, 反陣, 趷雞陣.

short_def: On structural drawings, B or BM may mean a beam (陣).
note: Xiaoluban: B / BM = beam, and warns that on survey drawings BM means benchmark. See 陣 and BM sense 2.

short_def: On survey and levelling drawings, BM means a benchmark: a fixed point of known reduced level. A site may also have a temporary benchmark (TBM).
note: Xiaoluban survey section, with an explicit warning that structural BM means beam. Unrelated to building management (usually BMS) unless the legend says otherwise. Other BM expansions were not locked in this pass.

short_def: A primary beam, usually spanning onto columns and supporting secondary beams.
note: A 2021 article: a large beam connecting to columns. Xiaoluban: 大陣／主陣 = girder.

short_def: A smaller beam spanning between primary beams.
note: Attested in a 2021 article.

short_def: The beam over a door or similar opening.
note: Attested in a 2021 article as 過門樑.

short_def: A beam that projects above the slab (an upstand), as opposed to a normal downstand beam at soffit level.
note: A 2021 article contrasts ordinary beams near the ceiling with 反陣 sitting on the floor above.

short_def: Slang for a cantilevered structure; a cantilever beam is 趷雞陣.
note: A 2021 article: 趷雞 = cantilever structure; 趷雞陣 = cantilever beam. Written form 趷 is the one given in that article; confirm locally if another character is preferred.

short_def: A wall hung from the structure above and not built up from the floor.
note: A 2021 article contrasts it with a normal wall built off the floor. Xiaoluban describes 懸吊牆 similarly, and warns that some drawing abbreviations for this idea are not standardised.

short_def: Slang for the heavy transfer plate between a podium (or lower floors) and the tower above.
note: A 2021 article: the transfer level between the lower floors and the tower of a large building. Formal English is transfer plate (sometimes transfer truss / transfer beam, which are different structural systems — do not blur them).

short_def: In a 2021 article, precast reinforced-concrete external wall panels.
note: Single informal source. The written form and etymology are not confirmed here (possibly from English 'facade', but that is a guess and is not stated in the source). Treat as low confidence until a second Hong Kong source or a drawing note confirms the spelling.

short_def: On the HKIE slang cards, 龍 is glossed as tunnel.
note: Specialist civil / tunnel-site usage. In ordinary Cantonese 龍 means dragon; only the engineering sense is recorded here. Single card source for this mapping, but the card set is a professional-institution publication.

short_def: The top of bedrock; rockhead.
note: HKIE cards: 石頭皮 / 岩石面 / rockhead.

short_def: The ordinary site word for a hole or opening in a wall, slab or hoarding.
note: A 2021 article writes 吼 and says it is pronounced 窿. This dataset prefers the transparent character 窿 and keeps 吼 as an attested alternative spelling. See also 獅山窿.

english: Hole left by a form-tie rod
short_def: The hole left in a concrete wall after a through-bolt (過山螺絲) is removed; it has to be made good.
note: A 2021 article writes 獅山吼 and says 吼 is to be pronounced 窿. This dataset uses 窿 as the transparent written form and keeps 吼 as an alternative spelling from that source.

short_def: In Hong Kong usage, 地下 is the ground floor (G/F), not a basement. This is the storey at street level.
note: A 2021 article stresses the contrast with Mainland floor numbering, where 一樓 is often the ground floor. On Hong Kong drawings this storey is usually G/F or 地下. See 一樓 and 地牢.

english: First floor (the storey above ground floor)
short_def: In Hong Kong, 一樓 is the floor above 地下 (i.e. 1/F), not the ground floor.
note: Important when talking with colleagues used to Mainland numbering. See 地下.

short_def: Site and everyday Hong Kong name for a basement, often an underground car park.
note: A 2021 article. Drawings usually say B1, B2 or 地庫.

short_def: A fan or blower, from English 'blower'. On building sites often a portable floor-standing ventilator.
note: HKIE cards: 寶路華 / 風機 / blower. JobsDB: a ventilating fan that can extract or blow. A 2021 article emphasises the portable site ventilator used in hot weather. In a plant room, 風機 may also mean a building-services fan in the ordinary technical sense.

short_def: A goods-only site hoist, from English 'hoist'. It must not be used to carry people.
note: JobsDB: no dual safety devices for passenger use, so people must not ride it. A 2021 article: a goods lift that cannot carry persons. Contrast 人𨋢 (passenger hoist).

formal_zh: 載人升降機／人貨升降機
short_def: The site hoist approved for carrying people, written with the Hong Kong character 𨋢 (from English 'lift').
note: A 2021 article writes 人（車立）, i.e. 人 + the combined character 𨋢. Contrast 開士機, which is goods-only. 𨋢 is standard written Cantonese for a lift.

short_def: Site name for a tower crane, from the balance-like silhouette of jib, cab and counterweight.
note: JobsDB explains the metaphor. A 2021 article notes the Mainland name 塔吊. Distinct from 街吊 (lorry-mounted mobile crane).

short_def: Slang for an excavator, from the way the bucket pecks at the ground like a chicken.
note: JobsDB and a 2021 article agree. Very widely used.

english: Compact loader (often a Bobcat-type skid-steer or similar)
short_def: A small site loader or similar compact machine, nicknamed 貓仔.
note: JobsDB: a small loading / earthmoving machine, associated with the Bobcat brand and cat-logo machines. A 2021 article says 'small bulldozer', which is looser. Prefer 'compact loader / skid-steer or similar small plant'; the brand name is a common but not exclusive reference.

short_def: Usually a mobile crane mounted on a lorry, used in the street or on site for shorter lifts.
note: A 2021 article. Distinct from 天秤 (tower crane).

short_def: The poker's vibrating head used to compact fresh concrete and drive out air.
note: A 2021 article and Xiaoluban agree (震筆／震棒).

short_def: A bent steel bar used for prising, especially when striking formwork.
note: A 2021 article: a bent bar for prising. Xiaoluban: pinch / stripping bar used by formwork carpenters.

short_def: Site slang for a machine used to compact soil, nicknamed a vibrating boat in one article.
note: Single 2021 source; the exact plant type (plate compactor vs roller) is not tightly specified. Medium confidence.

short_def: The adjustable head at the top of a scaffold or shoring prop, used to set height.
note: A 2021 article writes 馬蹓頭 for a height-adjusting scaffold fitting. Xiaoluban: 馬騮頭／底掌 = adjustable prop head / base (the base is 底掌 or 馬騮腳). Preferred written form in the compiled glossary is 馬騮頭.

short_def: A threaded rod tying two faces of wall formwork together; it is withdrawn when the forms are struck.
note: A 2021 article. The hole left behind is 獅山窿 (written 獅山吼 in that article, with 吼 to be read as 窿).

short_def: A powered scissor-type mobile elevating work platform. In Hong Kong, operators must have the required training.
note: A 2021 article notes the training requirement.

short_def: A spanner, from English 'spanner'.
note: Widely used Hong Kong rendering, also outside construction. Attested in a 2021 site-jargon article.

short_def: The usual site name for an oxy-acetylene (oxygen + acetylene) cutting or welding set.
note: A 2021 article also lists 風煤樽 (gas cylinders) and 風煤籠 (the cage used to store and lift the set).

english: Modular shoring / support frame (often used for access platforms too)
short_def: Modular steel framing used as falsework or as a temporary access structure; a 2021 article also mentions 現代通架 for modular towers used as site walkways.
note: Xiaoluban: 通架 = shoring / support frame erected before formwork and concreting. A 2021 article's 現代通架 appears to be a common modular-system name; do not treat it as the only brand. Deck pieces on top may be called 橋板.

short_def: In a 2021 article, 架餐 means tools or gear.
note: Single informal source; medium confidence. Written form follows that article.

short_def: Site slang for a valve, from English 'valve'. Also written 花奴.
note: HKIE cards: 嘩佬 / 花奴 / valve. Very common in BSE / plumbing / fire-service talk.

short_def: Site name for a star-delta motor starter.
note: HKIE cards: 九線掣 / 星角起動器 / star delta starter. (星角 = 星形-三角形.) Heard around plant rooms and temporary power.

formal_zh: 空調、消防、給排水、強弱電
english: The four common building-services trades: MVAC, fire services, plumbing and drainage, and electrical (including ELV)
short_def: A compact site phrase for the main building-services packages: air-conditioning / ventilation, fire services, water and drainage, and electrical (power and ELV).
note: A 2021 article spells out 空調、消防、給排水、強弱電. Closely related to 機電 / BS. Useful heading term for a BSI-oriented dictionary.

english: Building services / mechanical and electrical works
short_def: The usual Hong Kong umbrella term for building-services or mechanical-and-electrical packages, as opposed to civil or structural works.
note: A 2021 article says BS broadly means 機電工程. Xiaoluban: M&E = Mechanical & Electrical. In Hong Kong English, Building Services (BS) and E&M are both common; context may be a consultant discipline, a contractor package, or a drawing set. Abbreviation BS is a clash: British Standard (e.g. BS 8666 on rebar schedules) and, on survey / levelling notes, backsight. Some professional contexts also use BS for Building Surveyor (建築測量師) — that is a distinct official profession, not a drawing default. Always read the context. See headword BS.

alt_terms: 機電 | M&E | E&M | Building Services
short_def: In Hong Kong site and consultant talk, BS often means building-services or M&E works (機電).
note: See 機電. Clash: British Standard, and backsight on survey notes. Building Surveyor is a distinct profession sometimes also abbreviated BS; do not assume that reading on a drawing. Always read the context.

short_def: On specifications, rebar schedules and many product descriptions, BS plus a number means a British Standard (for example BS 8666 for bar bending).
note: Xiaoluban cites BS 8666 in the reinforcement section. Unrelated to building services unless the document is clearly a services package. See also BS as backsight.

short_def: In levelling / survey notes, BS means a backsight reading on a known point, used with foresight (FS) and sometimes intermediate sight (IS).
note: Xiaoluban survey section: BS / FS / IS = backsight / foresight / intermediate sight. Unrelated to Building Services or British Standard. See also BM (benchmark).

short_def: The ventilation and air-conditioning discipline or drawing set.
note: Standard Hong Kong professional abbreviation, used in ArchSD building-services specifications and on drawings. Xiaoluban lists the Chinese as 機械通風及空調.

short_def: A large air-handling unit that conditions and distributes supply air, usually in a plant room or on a roof.
note: Standard abbreviation on Hong Kong MVAC drawings and in ArchSD specifications. Not slang; included because a building-services inspector hears it constantly.

short_def: A local fan-coil terminal, typically at a ceiling or on a wall, serving a room or zone.
note: Standard Hong Kong MVAC abbreviation.

short_def: An air-handling unit that conditions outdoor (primary / fresh) air, often serving downstream fan-coil systems.
note: Standard Hong Kong MVAC abbreviation.

english: Variable Refrigerant Volume / Variable Refrigerant Flow
short_def: A multi-split refrigerant system in which one (or more) outdoor units serve many indoor units with variable refrigerant flow.
note: VRV began as a manufacturer trade name; VRF is the generic abbreviation. Both are used on Hong Kong sites and drawings.

short_def: On building-services drawings and in package talk, FS usually means fire-service installations.
note: Very common abbreviation clash. Other attested senses, recorded as separate rows: flat slab on structural drawings; far side on rebar drawings; foresight in levelling / survey notes (with BS / IS). Always read the legend. See also FSI and FS 251.

short_def: On structural drawings, FS may mean a flat slab (a slab supported directly on columns, without beams).
note: Xiaoluban records this structural sense and warns of the clash with Fire Services and far side. Always read the legend. See FS sense 1 (Fire Services).

short_def: On reinforcement drawings, FS may mean the far side of a member (as opposed to the near side).
note: Xiaoluban records this rebar-drawing sense. Always read the bar-mark conventions and the legend. See also FS as Fire Services, flat slab, or survey foresight.

short_def: In levelling / survey notes, FS means a foresight reading on an unknown point, as opposed to a backsight (BS) on a known point. Intermediate sights may be marked IS.
note: Xiaoluban survey section: BS / FS / IS = backsight / foresight / intermediate sight. Unrelated to Fire Services or flat slab. See also BM (benchmark) and BS (backsight).

short_def: The collective statutory term for fire service installations and equipment regulated by the Fire Services Department.
note: Used in FSD codes, circulars and certificates. Broader than 'sprinkler' alone.

formal_zh: 消防裝置及設備證明書
english: Certificate of Fire Service Installations and Equipment
short_def: The Fire Services Department certificate issued by a Registered Fire Service Installation Contractor after relevant FSI work, with a copy submitted to FSD.
note: Official form name: F.S. 251. A revised edition and online-submission arrangements have been announced in FSD circulars (including a 2025 revision). Always check the current FSD circular for the submission method in force.

short_def: The EMSD specified form certifying completion of an electrical installation, signed by the appropriate registered electrical worker / contractor.
note: EMSD Form WR1, Work Completion Certificate. Related: WR2 is the Periodic Test Certificate. Central to electrical T&C and handover on building projects.

short_def: The EMSD specified form certifying periodic inspection and testing of an electrical installation.
note: See also WR1, which is used at completion rather than at periodic test.

formal_zh: 建造、安裝、改動或拆除內部供水系統或消防供水系統申請書
english: Application for constructing, installing, altering or removing an inside service or fire service
short_def: The Water Authority form, typically submitted by a Licensed Plumber, seeking permission to construct, install, alter or remove an inside water service or a fire service.
note: WSD Form WWO 46. A staple of plumbing and fire-main site administration. Official English title as on the WSD form.

short_def: Site warning that a cable, metal part or other conducting object is live.
note: HKIE cards: 有氣 / 帶電 / electrically live. A 2021 article also uses 水氣 in a similar 'it's live — shock hazard' sense (see 水氣). This is a safety-critical phrase.

short_def: In a 2021 site-jargon article, 水氣 means that a wire, metal body or other medium is live and is a shock hazard.
note: Overlaps with 有氣, which is the form on the HKIE cards. Until more sources are compared, treat 水氣 as an attested alternative, not as a different electrical state. Unrelated to humidity or water vapour in ordinary language.

short_def: In electrical site talk recorded in 2021, 水線 means the earth wire, with green-and-yellow insulation.
note: Single informal source for this electrical sense. In other construction talk 水線 can also mean a water level line or a chalk/ink level line — that sense is not sourced here and should not be invented, but users should be aware that 線 names collide. Medium confidence.

short_def: The automatic fire-sprinkler installation, often just called 灑水 or 'sprinkler' on site.
note: Xiaoluban: 自動灑水系統 / sprinkler. A core FSI type, certificated under the FSD regime. Abbreviation SP can also mean Supervision Plan or soil pipe — see headword SP.

short_def: In fire-services documents and drawings, SP often means the automatic sprinkler system.
note: Xiaoluban warns that SP in site documents may instead mean Supervision Plan, and on drainage drawings Soil Pipe. See 灑水, 監工計劃書, and SP senses 2–3.

short_def: In statutory and site-administration documents, SP may mean the Supervision Plan submitted to the Building Authority before works commence.
note: See 監工計劃書. Clash with sprinkler and soil pipe. Always check the document type.

short_def: On drainage drawings, SP may mean a soil pipe: the pipe that carries soil (foul) drainage from water closets.
note: Xiaoluban drainage section records SP = soil pipe, and warns of the clash with sprinkler and Supervision Plan. Related to, but not the same as, SVP (soil and vent pipe).

english: Fire hydrant (and, in building talk, often the hydrant / hose-reel system)
short_def: A fire hydrant: a fixed outlet for the fire service to draw water. In building-services packages, 消防栓 may also refer to the building hydrant / hose-reel system.
note: Xiaoluban's short gloss is the hydrant as a fixed connection for firefighters. Building FH/HR systems are part of FSI. Do not assume street hydrant vs building in-riser without context.

short_def: On MVAC drawings, FD is usually a fire damper in a duct where it passes through a fire compartment.
note: Clash: on drainage drawings FD often means floor drain. Always check the discipline and the legend. Xiaoluban records both.

short_def: On drainage drawings, FD usually means a floor drain.
note: See FD sense 1 (fire damper) on MVAC drawings.

short_def: The plumbing and drainage package or drawing discipline.
note: Xiaoluban: P&D / D&P = Plumbing & Drainage.

short_def: A vertical stack that carries soil drainage and provides ventilation of the drainage system.
note: Standard drainage abbreviation on Hong Kong drawings.

short_def: In Hong Kong building-services talk, ELV usually means the extra-low-voltage package: access control, CCTV, structured cabling and similar systems, not merely the IEC voltage band in the abstract.
note: Xiaoluban's gloss matches this site usage. Official electrical-safety 'extra-low voltage' is a defined voltage range; the package name is broader in practice.

short_def: Building work carried out to allow building-services installation: openings, sleeves, bases, plinths and similar, often coordinated on combined builder's-work drawings.
note: Xiaoluban: 配合機電嘅建築工程 / Builder's Work In Connection (with services). Closely tied to combined builder's-work drawings (CBWD). A daily concern for a building-services inspector. Confirm the exact wording against the contract.

short_def: An electrical distribution board: the assembly that distributes circuits and houses protective devices.
note: Xiaoluban MEP section: 配電箱 / Distribution Board. Other expansions of DB exist in other disciplines; check the legend. Not locked as any other sense in this pass.

short_def: The testing and commissioning of an installation before handover, including functional tests, records and, where required, witness tests.
note: Standard Hong Kong building-services English. Architectural Services Department publishes a series of Testing and Commissioning Procedures for government buildings. Official Chinese wording is not locked here: ArchSD pages also use 測試及運作程序 for this series. Do not invent a single official Chinese form. Related informal talk (witness test, pressure test, flushing, isolation, 送電) is listed for a later pass.

short_def: The ordinary Hong Kong word for a construction site.
note: Universal. Used in compounds: 地盤三寶, 駐地盤工程師, 地盤指令.

short_def: The usual Hong Kong term for construction drawings or plans, including those approved by the Building Authority.
note: An approved 圖則 is a statutory reference document, not just a working sketch. Shop drawings are a related but different class (see 工場圖).

short_def: To place (pour) concrete into the formwork. A continuous placing operation is also called a pour.
note: One of the three core RC operations with 紮鐵 and formwork. Xiaoluban and workers' articles agree.

short_def: The process of cutting, bending and tying reinforcement to the drawings.
note: See 紮鐵佬 for the trade.

short_def: To remove formwork after the concrete has gained sufficient strength.
note: Xiaoluban: striking too early is dangerous and is controlled by specified times / strengths.

formal_zh: 缺陷修補／檢查清單修補
short_def: To inspect for and rectify outstanding defects, typically near completion, from a snag / defects list.
note: Xiaoluban: snagging / defects list. Everyday handover language on Hong Kong sites and in fitting-out.

english: Handover in vacant possession / hand over a cleared area
short_def: To hand over an area or premises cleared and vacant.
note: A 2021 article: 交付清空場地. The same phrase is widely used in Hong Kong property handover; on site it may mean a trade handing a cleared area to the next party.

short_def: In a 2021 site-jargon article, 起貨 means the work is finished / completed.
note: In ordinary shipping Chinese 起貨 can mean unloading cargo; the site sense here is completion. Single informal source for the site sense; medium confidence.

short_def: Colloquial name for the Occupation Permit issued by the Building Authority, without which a new building must not be occupied.
note: Statutory English: Occupation Permit (OP). New-building completion and OP application are typically made on Form BA13 (BA12 is used in temporary-occupation situations). The Building Authority must process an OP application within 14 days (Buildings Ordinance s.21). See also 臨時入伙紙 / TOP.

short_def: The official Buildings Department permit to occupy a new building, certifying that the works have been completed in accordance with the Ordinance and the approved plans.
note: See 入伙紙 for the colloquial name. Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP) is a separate, temporary permission (often Form BA12).

jyutping: lam4 si4 zim3 jung6 heoi2 ho2 zing3
short_def: A temporary permission to occupy a new building, or part of one, before a full Occupation Permit is issued.
note: Buildings Department Form BA12 covers certification of completion resulting in a new temporary building, or part of a new building, and application for a temporary occupation permit. Not a substitute for a full OP.

formal_zh: 同意展開工程／施工同意書
short_def: Colloquial name for the Building Authority's consent to commence and carry out building works, required after plan approval and before the works start.
note: Application is made on Form BA8 (application for consent to commence and carry out building works). Xiaoluban uses 施工同意書 / Commencement Consent. 開工紙 is the spoken name an inspector will actually hear.

formal_zh: 同意展開及進行建築工程申請書
english: Application for consent to commence and carry out building works
short_def: The Buildings Department specified form used to apply for consent to start building works.
note: See 開工紙. Form numbers and descriptions are as published by BD; always use the current specified form.

formal_zh: 新建建築物工程竣工證明書及佔用許可證申請書
english: Certificate on completion of building works resulting in a new building, and application for a permit to occupy such building
short_def: The usual Buildings Department form that certifies completion of a new building and applies for an Occupation Permit.
note: Processed with the OP application, generally within 14 days (BO s.21). See 入伙紙 / Occupation Permit. Official description as on the BD forms list.

formal_zh: 認可人士、註冊結構工程師及註冊岩土工程師作業備考
english: Practice Note for Authorized Persons, Registered Structural Engineers and Registered Geotechnical Engineers
short_def: Buildings Department practice notes that tell APs, RSEs and RGEs how the Building Authority administers the Buildings Ordinance in practice.
note: Numbered series (e.g. APP-13, APP-78). Everyday statutory-process jargon for anyone chasing approvals, consent or OP.

short_def: Building works that alter or add to an existing building, as administered by the Buildings Department, distinct from a new-building project.
note: Standard BD abbreviation, used on forms and practice notes. Completion pathways differ from a new-building OP (e.g. BA14 series).

short_def: The site-supervision plan that must be submitted to the Building Authority before works commence, under the Buildings Ordinance site-supervision regime.
note: Code of Practice for Site Supervision. Abbreviation SP is a three-way clash: Supervision Plan in statutory / site-admin documents; sprinkler in fire-services documents; soil pipe on drainage drawings. Always check the discipline and the legend. Linked to TCP grades. See also the headword SP.

jyutping: gin3 zuk1 si6 mou6 gaam1 duk1
short_def: The public officer (in practice the Director of Buildings) who administers the Buildings Ordinance, including plan approval, consent and occupation permits.
note: Not the same as 幫辦, 工程督察, or 工程監督. BA as a drawing or document abbreviation usually means Building Authority, including the BA form series (BA8, BA13). It is not Building Services (that's usually BS) and should not be read as Building Automation without a legend that says so. See also the headword BA.

short_def: On forms, practice notes and many site documents, BA means the Building Authority (建築事務監督), including the BA form series such as BA8 and BA13.
note: Not Building Services (usually BS) and not 幫辦. A further reading as Building Automation appears in some international BMS contexts; it was not locked here because it was not attested in the Hong Kong sources reviewed in this pass. Always check the document type and the legend. See 建築事務監督.

short_def: A formal written query from the contractor to the design team when the drawings, specification or site conditions are unclear or in conflict.
note: Standard contract-administration term on Hong Kong sites, recorded in Xiaoluban. Direction is contractor asks, designer answers.

short_def: An instruction changing the original contract works (adding, omitting or altering work), with cost and time consequences usually handled by the QS.
note: Everyday contract jargon. Related documents include CVI and architect's / engineer's instructions.

short_def: A written instruction from the supervisory side (architect or engineer) telling the contractor to carry out a stated action.
note: Xiaoluban also notes SI may be used for a supplemental instruction in some contract suites. Not the same as a Variation Order, though a site instruction may later give rise to a VO.

short_def: A request for the inspector or engineer to inspect a completed activity (for example rebar or formwork) before the next activity (for example concreting) may proceed.
note: Described in Xiaoluban as one of the documents front-line staff handle most often. Public-works sites may use a Request for Inspection and Survey Check (RISC) instead of or alongside a WIR.

short_def: A formal record that work or material does not meet the design or specification, requiring follow-up and rectification.
note: Quality-management term in daily site use.

jyutping: si1 gung1 fong1 faat3 can4 seot6 syu1
short_def: A document explaining how a particular activity will be carried out safely and in accordance with the requirements, usually submitted for approval before the work starts.
note: Often paired with a risk assessment. Standard Hong Kong (and wider) site-administration English.

alt_terms: Shop drawing | shop drawing | 施工詳圖
short_def: A contractor- or fabricator-prepared drawing, submitted for approval, showing how a portion of the works will actually be made or installed.
note: Xiaoluban uses SHOP DRAWING / Shop Drawing. Distinct from the consultant's contract or approved 圖則. Central to BSE installation packages.

english: Slinging / preparing a load for lifting
short_def: To prepare, sling and bind a load for crane lifting.
note: A 2021 article: 埋碼 is the slinging / binding work; 埋碼員 is the worker who does it, equated there with 叻架佬. Silver-card / specified-trade training may apply.

short_def: To carry out rock blasting. 爆石 is also used for blasting or breaking rock.
note: HKIE cards list both 燒炮 / blasting and 爆石. Highly regulated; not casual slang for any noisy work.

short_def: The regular (often weekly) progress meeting with sub-contractors.
note: A 2021 article also records the coarse pejorative nickname 爛仔會. That alias is attested but is not a neutral workplace term and should not be indexed as a public look-up lemma by default. If shown at all, label it as pejorative. Recommended public default: filter the alias; keep 判頭會 as the headword. Owner accepted this public default on 25 November 2026: filter the alias 爛仔會; keep 判頭會 as the headword.

english: To visit a factory (often in the Mainland) for inspection or discussion
short_def: To go to a works or factory to inspect production or discuss fabrication, often meaning a Mainland plant in Hong Kong project talk.
note: A 2021 article. Common in precast, facade, and plant-equipment off-site inspection talk. 廠 is the factory, not a Hong Kong plant room (機房).

short_def: The temporary hoarding that fences a site off from the public street.
note: A 2021 article: 工地圍牆. Xiaoluban: hoarding, which must comply with regulations. Related: 人閘 (pedestrian gate), 車閘 (vehicle gate).

english: Pedestrian site gate / personnel access in the hoarding
short_def: The pedestrian opening in the site hoarding used as the workers' entrance.
note: A 2021 article. Contrast 車閘.

english: Vehicle site gate in the hoarding
short_def: The vehicular opening in the site hoarding.
note: A 2021 article. Contrast 人閘.

english: Site office, store or rest area (container, shed, etc.)
short_def: A loosely used name for an indoor place on site where people can office, rest, change or store personal things, such as a site container or temporary shed.
note: A 2021 article says helmets may come off inside a 架步 but must be worn once outside. Informal.

short_def: Scaffolding for access and materials, in Hong Kong typically bamboo or metal.
note: Xiaoluban: 棚 / scaffold / 棚架. Safety requirements are strict. See 棚佬.

short_def: The fall or gradient given to a floor or drainage surface so that water runs to the outlet.
note: A 2021 article: 地面排水傾斜度. Everyday finishing and drainage speech.

english: Building works (as opposed to civil works)
short_def: A rough Cantonese rendering of English 'building', used for building (architectural) works as opposed to civil works.
note: A 2021 article: 諧音，房建工程. Informal discipline slang; pair with 斯否 (civil). Medium confidence; pronunciation-based writing.

short_def: A rough Cantonese rendering of English 'civil', used for civil-engineering works. Municipal works in Hong Kong are also treated as civil.
note: A 2021 article itself calls the rendering inexact (不太準的諧音). Pair with 標頂. Medium confidence.

short_def: A contemptuous name for a poor-quality weld.
note: A 2021 article. Coarse but widely understood as a quality criticism, not a process name.
